neighbours.label: A negated perfect with 'even' or 'yet' ("hasn't even started yet", "had not even begun") that sets up a contrast clause (and already / but / yet …); fires on even / yet / the following comma or conjunction
fire: The paint hasn't even dried yet and the kids are already drawing on the wall.
We had not even unpacked the car, but the neighbours were at the door with a pie.
The baby hasn't even been born yet and her room is full of toys.
He has not even read the report, yet he is sure it is wrong.
The store hadn't even opened yet and a line stretched around the block.
I haven't even had my coffee and the phone is already ringing.
The match had not even started, but the crowd was on its feet.
They haven't even met yet and she already dislikes him.
quiet: The paint dried quickly and the kids are drawing on the paper we gave them.
We unpacked the car, and the neighbours came to the door with a pie.
The baby was born in March and her room is full of toys.
He read the report twice, and he is sure it is wrong.
The store opened at nine and a line stretched around the block.
I had my coffee on the porch and then the phone started ringing.
The match started on time, and the crowd was on its feet.
They met last year at a wedding and she still dislikes him.

notes: Card: ' yet', ' even', ',', ' but' after 'not even started', 'hadn't even seen it'; output promotes ' but', ' yet', '—but'. Probes: four not-even(-yet) sentences 0.32-0.84, 'hadn't left but' 0.40; affirmative versions 0.01-0.02, "I don't even like yogurt" 0.17.
